notes: Seasonal dog ban from 1st July to 31st August, 10am-6pm. No lifeguards; visitors must be aware of the tide to avoid getting cut off.

location: Cadgwith Cove Beach, Cadgwith, Cornwall TR12 7JZ
notes: Dogs banned from the beach in July and August between 10am and 6pm. A short walk to The Devil’s Frying Pan, a rock arch and hole formed from a collapsed cave in the 1800s.

Dogs are welcome on Cawsand Bay except between 1 July - 31 August when a seasonal dog ban is in place between 10am and 6pm. The beach is near the 17th Century fishing villages of Cawsand and Kingsand.
Seasonal dog ban from 15 May to 30 September, 10am-6pm. Lifeguards patrolling from May to September, 10am-6pm. Family-friendly beach with excellent surf conditions and a Blue Flag award since 2005.

Beach access at Bedruthan is closed due to cliff falls in May 2021 and January 2021. Steps are expected to remain closed with no confirmed timescale. National Trust shop open 28 May to 31 Oct. Café and tea garden available.

Perranporth Beach is RNLI lifeguarded from early April to late October. Dogs are allowed all year. The beach offers surfing, swimming, snorkeling, and water sports. There is a welcome café halfway along the walk and a bar nearby. The beach is accessible and has a bar close by. The Saint on the Sands is a local legend about Saint Piran's arrival in Cornwall.
Dogs banned on the beach from 15 May to 30 September 2023, 10am-6pm. Lifeguards patrol from Easter to end of October 2023. Seasonal beach cafe and ice cream kiosk available.

A hidden gem, this scenic tidal inlet near Tintagel is well worth the steep steps, though not suitable for wheelchairs or push chairs. No lifeguard coverage. Revealed only at low tide, it becomes one with Benoath Cove. Home to Elephant Rock and caverns.

Portreath Beach has a seasonal dog ban from 1 July to 31 August, 10am-6pm. Lifeguards are on patrol from 10am-6pm, mid-May to last weekend of September. The beach is a popular sandy cove for swimmers, surfers, and sunbathers.

location: Carbis Bay Beach, St Ives, Cornwall, TR26 2NP
notes: Seasonal dog ban from 15 May to 30 September, 10am-6pm. Free for all visitors. Calm waters ideal for swimming. Hosted the 47th G7 summit in 2021.

location: Carne Beach, The Roseland, Cornwall TR2 5AG
notes: Carne Beach is a National Trust-owned beach on the Roseland Peninsula, known for its golden sands and shingle shoreline. It is dog-friendly all year round but requires close control. Access is via narrow lanes, and there is no overnight camping. A seasonal beach cafe and ice cream kiosk are available.

location: Gyllyngvase Beach, Cliff Road, Falmouth, Cornwall, TR11 4NA
notes: Seasonal dog restriction: 10am-6pm from 15 May to 30 September. Dogs on leads allowed on rocks year-round. Family-friendly beach with soft sands, rock pools, and lifeguards summer months. Blue Flag and Seaside Awards. Connected to Queen Mary Gardens and the south-west coastal path.

location: Godrevy Beach, Gwithian, Hayle, Cornwall, TR27 5ED
notes: Godrevy Beach is a sandy cove that joins with Gwithian Beach at low tide to create one immense, golden crescent. It has spectacular views of St Ives and Godrevy Lighthouse. The beach is part of the Godrevy to Portreath Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. The RNLI Lifeguards are based at Hayle.

Dogs are welcome all year round at Mother Ivey’s Bay, though they must be kept on a lead between 10am and 6pm. The bay is privately owned but freely accessible from the South West Coast Path. No parking is available at the bay itself.

Polzeath Beach has a seasonal dog ban from 15 May to 30 September, 10am to 6pm. It is RNLI lifeguarded from early May to late September, with additional patrols during school holidays and some weekends. The beach is located in Cornwall, PL27 6SS.

Whitsand Bay offers over three miles of golden sand from Rame Head to Portwrinkle. It is a hidden gem, never crowded, with rock pools and a popular dive site. The bay is home to HMS Scylla, an ex-naval frigate sunk in 2004 to form an artificial reef.
RNLI Lifeguards patrol from mid-May to the last weekend of September. Dog-friendly all year round. Film locations include 'In Die Another Day' and 'House of the Dragon'.
Seasonal dog ban from 15 May to 30 September, 10am-6pm. Lifeguards patrol 10am-6pm during summer. Pay and display car park available. Roadside parking on Mill Ball Hill.
Seasonal dog ban from 10am to 6pm in July and August. No lifeguards, but surf rescue equipment is present. Sand visible only at low tide. Safe swimming from slipway. Poldark scenes filmed here.
Prussia Cove is a secluded beach in Cornwall, known for its history as a smugglers' den. Swimming is allowed on calm days at high tide, but no lifeguards are present. Dogs are welcome all year round.

Seasonal dog ban from 15 May to 30 September, 10am-6pm. Lifeguards patrol from Easter to November, 10am-6pm. Surfing and swimming are popular activities. The beach is sandy and has a gentle slope into the surf.

location: Chapel Bar Beach, Padstow, Cornwall, PL28 8DB
notes: Chapel Bar Beach lies at the mouth of the River Camel in North Cornwall, just a 10-minute walk from Padstow. It stretches for around 1½ miles along the Camel Estuary and offers views of Daymer Bay. The 'Doom Bar' sand bank protects the estuary from the Atlantic and is linked to folklore of a mermaid's curse. The beach is submerged at high tide, and the 'Doom Bar' has been responsible for over 600 shipwrecks since records began.

Seasonal dog ban from 10am to 6pm between July 1st and August 31st. Dogs on leads allowed on the rocks year-round. Popular for diving and snorkelling due to wartime U-boat wreckage. Access via sloping path and steps from the main road.
Seasonal dog ban from 1 July to 31 August, 10am-6pm. Lifeguards patrol from mid-May to last weekend of September. Minack Theatre is a 10-minute walk from the beach. Not wheelchair friendly.

location: Gorran Haven, St Austell, Cornwall, PL26 6JG
notes: Gorran Haven Beach is a small sandy beach at the edge of the quaint coastal village south of Mevagissey on the edge of St Austell Bay. It is partially sheltered by its historic stone quay, making its crystal clear waters a favourite local spot for swimming and kayaking. The beach is dog friendly, however they must be kept on leads. Nearby, The Dodman headland, with its Iron Age hillfort is well worth exploring.

location: Charlestown Beach, Charlestown, St Austell, Cornwall, PL25 3NJ
notes: Dogs banned from 1st April to 31st October; welcome the rest of the time. Quayside popular for Poldark filming. Shipwreck Treasure Museum and cafes nearby.

Hannafore Beach is a quiet shingle beach with sandy stretches and rock pools. It is a popular dog-walking spot year-round. Two seasonal cafes, a putting green, and tennis courts are available. The beach is accessible via a long sea wall with free parking above. Looe Island, a marine nature reserve, is nearby and reachable by boat from the harbour. Regular rockpooling rambles are organized by the local Marine Conservation group throughout the year.

location: Hawker's Cove Beach, Padstow, Cornwall, PL28 8HW
notes: Hawker's Cove Beach is off the beaten track, accessible via the South West Coast Path from Padstow. It features a small tea shop and is historically significant as the former RNLI Padstow Lifeboat Station. The beach passes Gun Point with Napoleonic war fortifications and is near Daymer Bay. The Doom Bar sand bank is a notable hazard. The area is accessible year-round.

location: Downderry Beach, Downderry, Looe, Cornwall, PL11 3JR
notes: Downderry Beach is a long, expansive grey sand and shingle beach about five miles east of Looe. It is dog-friendly throughout the year and popular for swimming, fishing, and snorkeling. At low tide, the beach’s rock pools are exposed for exploration. The South West Coast Path runs through the village, though there is no safe access back up the cliffs. The village has a general store, pub, and café.

Constantine Bay is a popular surf spot in North Cornwall, known for its left and right waves. It has a rocky reef at the southern end and is bordered by sand dunes. Lifeguards are on duty from 1st May to 26th September and over weekends from Easter to the end of October. The beach is suitable for experienced surfers due to hidden rocks and strong rips. It is a west-facing beach with a reputation for producing top quality waves.

Dogs banned 10am-6pm from 15 May to 30 September; dogs on leads allowed year-round. Beach cafe and ice cream kiosk available. Lifeguards from mid-May to last weekend of September. Sand chairs for disabled visitors. Contact: 01288 352226 (June-September), rnli.org, tel: 01288 354240.
Dog ban in place all year long. Sand chairs available for hire. Beach is a Cornish classic with golden sands and gentle waves. Located in Looe, Cornwall, PL13 1HL.

location: Gwithian Towans Beach, Hayle, Cornwall, TR27 5BX
notes: Gwithian Towans Beach is part of Three Mile Beach in St Ives Bay. It features sand dunes, cliffs, and rock pools. Grey seals are often spotted nearby. The beach is popular with surfers and kite surfers due to consistent swell. It is accessible year-round with a strong sea breeze.
Dogs are welcome on Housel Bay except during July and August (10am - 6pm) when a seasonal dog ban is in place. Accessible via the South West Coast Path from Lizard Point at low tide.

location: Chapel Porth Beach, St Agnes, Cornwall, TR5 0NT
notes: Dogs are welcome except July and August (10am-6pm). Lifeguard cover May to September. Free car park for National Trust members. No overnight camping. Cafe available with ice cream and views.

location: Helford Passage Beach, Helford, Cornwall TR11 5LB
notes: Helford Passage Beach is a picturesque estuary beach in Cornwall, accessible at low tide. It is located on the north side of the estuary, near the Ferry Boat Inn, and serves as a popular launching point for motor boats and small yachts. The beach is also a great spot for walking along the South West Coast Path towards Glendurgan and Trebah.

location: Gunwalloe Church Cove Beach, Helston, Cornwall, TR12 7QG
notes: Seasonal dog ban from 10am to 6pm in July and August. Lifeguards patrol during summer. National Trust owned, archaeological and geological significance. Features a medieval church with a bell tower.
Dogs are allowed all year round on Eastern Green beach. Summer dog bans apply to Longrock Beach. Accessible via the South West Coast Path due to proximity of the railway line.

Gwynver Beach is a secluded stretch of golden sand in Cornwall, named after Guinevere. It is an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty, accessible via an arduous path through sand dunes. The beach features rocky headlands and the South West Coast Path. Life guards are on duty from May to September 2023. Parking is available above the beach or at Sennen Cove.

Hemmick Beach is a secluded, sandy south-west facing beach surrounded by rolling pasture and dramatic rocky headlands. It can only be accessed by a steep narrow road from Boswinger, near Gorran Haven. The beach is wild and untamed, with tiny coves and rock pools to explore at low tide. Less than a mile away is The Dodman, a high headland with an Iron Age fortification and a granite cross.

location: Coverack Beach, The Lizard, Cornwall, TR12 6SP
notes: Coverack beach is dog friendly, but dogs must be kept on leads during June, July and August (2023). There is also a small rocky beach at Perprean Cove to the south of the village.

Crantock Beach is dog friendly but dogs must be under control. Lifeguards are on duty from May to September. The River Gannel creates dangerous currents, so swimming near the river is not advised. The beach is accessible via a level path from the National Trust car park. Cafes, toilets, and parking are nearby.

location: Harlyn Bay Beach, Padstow, Cornwall, PL28 8SQ
notes: Harlyn Bay is a family-friendly beach with golden sand and rock pools. Lifeguards are on duty from May to September and weekends until October half-term. Surfing conditions are best when swells are big on west-facing beaches with southwest winds. The beach has a small stream leading to it and an iron age cemetery with over 130 graves. Harlyn Surf School offers surfing, coasteering, stand up paddleboarding, and guided kayak tours.

Duckpool Beach is a wild, pebble and rock-lined beach with a sandy shoreline exposed at low tide. It is a National Trust site, four miles north of Bude, where the Coombe Valley meets the sea. The beach features lichens, maritime grasses, and wildflowers. It has a 100-metre-high Steeple Point Cliff. Anti-tank blocks from WW2 are present. Dangerous currents make swimming unsuitable. A National Trust car park is available, free to members. No overnight camping allowed. Dogs are allowed all year round but must be kept under control.

location: Great Western Beach, Newquay, Cornwall TR7 2NE
notes: Lifeguards are stationed from 10am-6pm between 18th May and 29th September 2024. Dogs are allowed all year. A section of Great Western has been cordoned off following a cliff fall.

Hayle Towans beach is a vast expanse of golden sand backed by sand dunes, part of Hayle’s 'Three Mile Beach' within St Ives Bay. It joins with neighbouring bays at low tide and is known for its wild dunes, Atlantic swell, and year-round popularity. The village of Phillack lies half a mile inland, home to the Bucket of Blood pub with a smuggling legend.

Daymer Bay Beach is a sheltered bay within the Camel Estuary, ideal for swimming, paddling, and kitesurfing. It offers views of the Camel Estuary and access to Brea Hill and St Enodoc Church. Perfect for families.

Fistral Beach in Newquay, Cornwall (TR7 1HY) is known for its surfing and scenic beauty. Lifeguard cover is in place from Easter to end of October on Fistral Beach and from 10th July to 5th September (2022) on South Fistral Beach. Sand chairs are available for hire and provided by Cornwall Mobility in partnership with Disability Cornwall and Isles of Scilly.

Nansidwell Beach is a quiet, secluded cove west of historic Falmouth. It is privately owned and offers snorkelling, diving, and swimming. The beach is dog-friendly, but visitors must be mindful of others and take waste with them.

Dogs are welcome except during July and August (10am to 6pm) on the main beach. A seasonal dog ban applies. The beach has a cafe, car parking, public toilets, and watersports activities. No RNLI lifeguard presence. The 'Ben Asdale' shipwreck is visible off shore.

Lansallos Beach is a tranquil sheltered bay managed by the National Trust, located a few miles west of Polperro. It is reached by walking down an uneven path from the NT carpark in Lansallos village. The beach has no facilities and requires dogs to be under control.

location: Polridmouth Cove Beach, Fowey, Cornwall, PL23 1EB
notes: Polridmouth Cove Beach is a quiet sheltered cove separating into two bays at high tide. It has a history of seawater baths and ornamental lakes used as decoys in WW2. Daphne du Maurier inspired her novel Rebecca from this beach. The South West Coast Path passes here, offering views from Fowey to St Austell.
Dogs are welcome on the beach except July and August, 10am-6pm. Mousehole is a fishing village with two sandy beaches and a pebble beach. It has a rock pool and free parking.

Kenneggy Sands Beach is a secluded and unspoilt bay between Helston and Penzance, accessible at low tide via the South West Coast Path. It has a rich smuggling history and is surrounded by cliffs and cottages.

Pendower Beach is a National Trust-owned beach on the Roseland Peninsula, part of Cornwall's National Landscape. It joins with Carne at low tide to form over a mile of golden shoreline. The beach is surrounded by low soft cliffs and rock pools designated as SSSIs. The village of Veryan is about a mile inland, and the Nare Hotel offers afternoon teas on the lawns.

location: Par Sands Beach, St Austell, Cornwall, PL25 5DS
notes: Par Sands Beach is a wide sandy expanse backed by low dunes near the village of Par, four miles from St Austell. It is a popular dog-walking beach year-round and a good kite-surfing and windsurfing beach due to southwesterly winds.

location: Mullion Cove beach, Mullion, Cornwall, TR12 7EP
notes: Mullion Cove is a small sandy beach on the west coast of the Lizard Peninsula, mostly covered at high tide. It is located beside the historic lifeboat station and Mullion harbour, which is a working harbour and protects a fleet of small boats from the Atlantic. The area is owned and cared for by the National Trust, and the Victorian harbour was originally built in the 1890s.

location: Pentewan Beach, West End, Pentewan, St Austell, Cornwall, PL26 6BX
notes: Pentewan Beach is a family-friendly, sheltered bay with white shingle sand and clear waters. It is privately owned, and dog policies may change; check with the holiday park. The beach is backed by a large holiday park and features a former railway line as a walking and cycle path.
Dogs banned 10am-6pm July-August 2023 on main beach; sand chairs available. Lifeguard cover 8 July to 3 September 2023. Access to St Michael's Mount via granite causeway at low tide.
Dogs are welcome except between 1st July and 31st August (10am - 6pm). Lifeguard cover from mid-May to last weekend of September. Access via steps or slipway. Seasonal dog ban applies.

location: Lusty Glaze Beach Road, Newquay, Cornwall TR7 3AE
notes: Lusty Glaze Beach is a privately owned sandy beach on the edge of Newquay, sheltered by high cliffs. It is dog-friendly all year-round and has a bar and restaurant with views. Lifeguard cover is from July to September 2023. The beach offers adventure activities like climbing, abseiling, and jet skiing.

Dogs are banned from the eastern part of the beach during July and August (10am-6pm). The beach is popular for swimming, windsurfing, and is accessible from Penzance. Lifeguards are present during the summer months.

Northcott Mouth is a rocky cove on the north coast with sandy shore and rock pools at low tide. It has no toilet facilities and a summer tea caravan. Lifeguard cover is available in summer. Dogs are welcome.
Discussion about banning dogs on the beach in summer months (Feb 2023). Village has cafes, shops, pubs, and a car park.

location: Mexico Towans Beach, Hayle, Cornwall TR27 5AG
notes: Mexico Towans Beach is a remote stretch of sand between Hayle and Gwithian, known for its towans and wildlife. It is an SSSI and spans approximately 400 hectares.

Polurrian Cove has a dog ban from 1st July to 31st August between 10am - 6pm. Dogs on leads are permitted on the rocks year-round. The beach is within walking distance of Mullion, the largest village on the Lizard Peninsula. It is located in a designated Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty and a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI).

Mawgan Porth is a tranquil cove between Newquay and Padstow, offering good surf and coastal views. Lifeguard cover is from 29 April to 24 September 2023, and weekends in October. Sand chairs are available from Betty's News and Cornwall Mobility.

location: Poldhu Cove Beach, Mullion, Cornwall, TR12 7HZ
notes: Dogs are welcome except between 1 July and 31 August (10am - 6pm). The beach is part of Cornwall's National Landscape and home to the Marconi Centre. Lifeguards are present between mid-May and the last weekend of September.

location: Loe Bar Beach, Helston, Cornwall TR13 9DZ
notes: Loe Bar beach is a half mile sand and shingle bank separating The Loe, Cornwall’s largest natural freshwater lake, from the sea. It is dog-friendly year-round and accessible via the South West Coast Path from Porthleven or Helston, where bike hire is available.

Dogs are welcome on Kennack Sands Beach except during July and August (10am - 6pm) when a seasonal dog ban is in place. Lifeguard cover from mid-May to the last weekend of September. Part of the Lizard National Nature Reserve, known for its geological features and surfing.

Lantic Bay is a hidden gem in the Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty, known for its crystal-clear waters and white sand. Access involves walking along a steep rocky path, and there are no lifeguards, toilets, or refreshments. It is not suitable for buggies.

location: Lamorna Cove Beach, Penzance, Cornwall TR19 6XH
notes: Lamorna Cove Beach has a seasonal café and a pub further up the valley. No lifeguard cover or public toilets. Car park is privately owned and monitored by ANPR cameras. Parking is cash only.

Porthleven Beach is three glorious miles of golden sand and steeply shelving shingle running east from the historic harbour. It’s not recommended to swim along this beach, but when the tide is out, you can walk along the vast shoreline to Loe Bar, Cornwall’s largest freshwater lake. RNLI Lifeguards patrol the beach during the summer months.

location: Seaton Beach, Nr Looe, Cornwall, PL13 1PX
notes: Seaton Beach is a family-favourite with easy access and parking. It's popular with dog walkers and offers good waves for surfing. Lifeguards patrol between May and September. Behind the beach is Seaton Valley Country Park, home to wildlife like dragonflies, butterflies, ducks, kingfishers, dormice, and otters. The main path is flat and leads deep into the valley.

Portholland Beach features two secluded coves with a granite sea wall. Low tide connects the coves into a sandy shoreline. The Roseland Peninsula is part of Cornwall's National Landscape, known for its natural beauty and mild climate.

location: Porth Kidney Sands, St Ives, Cornwall TR26 3GN
notes: Dog friendly all year, but dogs must be on a lead on the footpath from St Uny Church to the beach. Lifeguard cover from 8 July to 3 September 2023. Swimming not recommended in the mouth of the Hayle Estuary.

location: Porthoustock Beach, St Keverne, The Lizard, Cornwall, TR12 7NQ
notes: Porthoustock Beach, known locally as ‘Pro'stock,’ is an east-facing pebble beach with a large expanse of coarse grey sand and shingle revealed at low tide. It is a popular area for divers with many shipwrecks to be explored around the treacherous reef, The Manacles. Swimming should be done with care. Parking is allowed at the back of the beach, taking care not to obstruct the boats of the local fishermen. There are toilets behind the beach and some picturesque thatched cottages.

location: Porthgwidden Beach, St Ives, Cornwall TR26 1PL
notes: Dogs are welcome on this beach except from 1st July to 31st August between 10am and 6pm. The beach is normally safe for swimming unless the winds are easterly.

location: Readymoney Cove Beach, Fowey, Cornwall, PL23 1EB
notes: Dogs are welcome except between July 1st and August 31st (10am-6pm) when a seasonal dog ban is in place. There's a small cafe/shop and toilets.

Rock beach is a vast stretch of golden sands and turquoise sea on the shore of the Camel Estuary, opposite Padstow. It is a popular spot for swimmers and sun-seekers, and offers coastal routes to Daymer Bay and Polzeath. A small ferry connects Rock to Padstow. The beach is family-friendly and allows dogs on leads year-round.

location: Portscatho Beach, Portscatho, The Roseland, Cornwall, TR2 5LW
notes: Dogs are welcome on this beach except between 1st July and 31st August (10am-6pm) when a seasonal dog ban is in place. (2023)

Sandymouth Beach is an untouched pebble and sand beach on the wild north coast. It features a waterfall and geological formations, including fossilised plant remains and 300-million-year-old rock formations. The beach is a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI). Lifeguards patrol during summer months.

location: Porth Joke Beach, Newquay, Cornwall, TR8 5EQ
notes: Porth Joke Beach, known locally as ‘Polly Joke,’ is a small but beautiful north-west facing cove owned by the National Trust. It features wild rocky outcrops, a sandy beach, undulating headlands, turquoise sea, and craggy cliff-faces. The beach is a popular spot for walking the South West Coast Path and is remote, attracting only the most dedicated beachgoers.

location: Porthluney Cove Beach, Caerhays, Mevagissey, Cornwall, PL26 6LY
notes: Dog friendly all year, but on leads from April-October. No lifeguard cover. Seasonal pop-up cafes, picnic area, and toilets available. Located in front of the daily charge car park. Accessible via the daily charge car park. Popular with locals for swimming and beach games. Offers a striking backdrop with Caerhays Castle and Gardens nearby.

Port Gaverne is a sheltered cove with sand at low tide, near Port Isaac. It is a National Trust site with rock pools and historical significance as a port for slate and coal. The name originates from 'Karn Hun' meaning rocky haven. It appears in the TV series Doc Martin.

location: Portwrinkle Beach, Crafthole, Nr. Torpoint, Cornwall, PL11 3BP
notes: Dogs banned 10am-6pm during July and August on Portwrinkle Beach. Small café and parking available. Hoodny Cove and Finnygook beach are nearby, both serene and popular for surfers.

location: Porthminster Beach, St Ives, Cornwall TR26 2BN
notes: Dogs banned 10am-6pm from 15 May to 30 September; sand chairs available from the cafe. Lifeguards patrol 10am-6pm between 18 May and 29 September. Located near St Ives Centre with cafes, shops, and art galleries.

location: Praa Sands Beach, Penzance, Cornwall TR20 9TQ
notes: Dogs banned from 10am-6pm between July 1st and August 31st (2023). Full lifeguard cover from 29th April to 24th September, with weekend cover from 30th September to 15th October and half-term cover from 21st to 29th October. Seasonal dog ban applies.

location: Porthcurnick Beach, Portscatho, The Roseland, Cornwall, TR2 5EW
notes: Porthcurnick Beach is a National Trust-owned beach on the Roseland Peninsula, known for its rock pools and water activities. It is located just north of Portscatho and is a family-friendly destination within Cornwall’s Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty.

location: Porthpean Beach, St Austell, Cornwall, PL25 3RD
notes: Dogs are welcome except between July 1st and 31st August (10am-6pm) when a seasonal dog ban is in place. Toilets are available. Access is on a steep incline from a privately run car park.

location: Porthchapel Beach, St Levan, Nr Porthcurno, Cornwall, TR19 7AA
notes: Dogs banned from 1 May to 30 September (8am to 7pm) below the mean high tide line; allowed above the line year-round. Includes St Levan holy well and medieval chapel.

location: Portheras Cove, St Just, Cornwall, TR19 7DN
notes: Portheras Cove is a secluded beach with unstable cliffs and rockfall risks. No lifeguard, no public facilities. SSSI area with wildlife, and no mobile/wifi. Accessible via Pendeen Lighthouse and South West Coast Path.

location: TR19 7NN, St Just in Penwith, Cornwall
notes: Priest Cove is a small fishing bay with a quaint slipway, located in the crook of the Cape, overlooking imposing cliffs. It is part of the Cornish Mining World Heritage Site and is owned and cared for by the National Trust.

Dogs banned 10am-6pm from 1 July to 31 August 2024 on the main beach. Lifeguards patrol 10am-6pm between 18 May and 29 September 2024. Porth Island (Trevelgue Head) is a historic landmark with archaeological significance dating back to the Mesolithic period.

location: Porthcothan Bay Beach, Padstow, Cornwall, PL28 8LW
notes: Porthcothan Beach is dog friendly with no seasonal ban. Lifeguards are on duty from 13 May to 24 September 2023. Parking and facilities are nearby. The beach is connected to the Poldark filming locations.

location: St Ives Harbour, St Ives, Cornwall TR26 1LG
notes: Dogs are welcome on the beach except between 1st July and 31st August (10am - 6pm) when a seasonal dog ban is in place. The beach is bordered by stone piers, and small boats can be launched from the slipway at the north end of the harbour, though access is difficult during the summer season.

Watergate Bay is a vast stretch of sand with big Atlantic swells and high sea-beaten cliffs, considered one of Cornwall's best beaches. It is around 3 miles from Newquay on the North Cornwall coast, stretching for two miles of golden sand, imposing cliffs, and untamed sea. The beach is dog-friendly year-round and has cafes and restaurants nearby for shelter and warmth.

location: Upton Towans Beach, Hayle, Cornwall TR27 5AX
notes: Upton Towans Beach is located to the north of Hayle, spanning three miles on the eastern side of St Ives Bay. It is ideal for surfing and safe for bathing, backed by sand dunes known as towans. Lifeguard cover is from 13 May to 24 September 2023. Dogs are allowed all year round.

location: Towan Beach - The Roseland, Bohortha, The Roseland, Cornwall, TR2 5LW
notes: Towan Beach is a quiet, south-east facing sand and shingle bay near St Mawes. It is dog-friendly year-round and located within an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. The beach is accessible via the South West Coast Path and is near the historic St Anthony’s Head Lighthouse.

location: Talland Bay Beach, Polperro, Cornwall, PL13 2JA
notes: Talland Bay Beach is located between Looe and Polperro. It features two coves, Talland Sands and Rotterdam Beach, with crystal-clear sea and rock pools. Seasonal toilets are near the main beach, and cafes are available at both coves. Access is via narrow lanes with limited parking.

Summerleaze Beach is RNLI lifeguarded, patrolled from 4th May to 29th September 10am-6pm, and during Easter school holidays and October half-term. Dogs must be on leads from 21st May to 30th September 10am-6pm. Disabled access, toilets, and sand chairs are available. The beach has a sea pool opened in 1930 and is within five minutes of Bude centre.

Treyarnon Bay is a clean, north-west facing sandy beach surrounded by low cliffs and backed by sand dunes. It is popular for its expanse of fine sand, rock pools, and tidal pool. The South West Coast Path runs through the area, offering views and a spot for hikers. It is a family-friendly beach with consistent surf waves.

Widemouth Bay is an RNLI lifeguarded beach patrolled from 10am to 6pm between 4th May and 29th September, and during Easter school holidays, October half-term, and weekends between 20th April - 28th April and 5th October and 20th October. Dogs are banned between May 15th and September 30th, 10am to 6pm.

Trevaunance Cove Beach is the main beach near St Agnes, Cornwall. It offers wild cliffs, sandy cove, and historical significance with Mesolithic and Bronze Age evidence. The beach is accessible from the village and has rock pools and climbing opportunities.

Towan Beach is Newquay’s most sheltered beach, protected by the harbour. It is located at the bottom of a steeply sloping hill, bordered by the harbour to the west and 'The Island' to the east. The beach is accessible at low tide, joining with other coves to form a single expanse of golden sand.

Dogs banned 10am-6pm from 15 May to 30 September 2024 on the main beach; dogs on leads permitted on the rocks year-round. Lifeguarded between 10am-6pm daily from 18 May to 29 September 2024. Seasonal beach cafe and ice cream kiosk available.

Trebarwith Strand is a dog-friendly beach at the base of cliffs, offering wildlife watching and coastal views. Lifeguards are required for swimming due to dangerous currents. Located 2 miles south-west of Tintagel.

Carlyon Bay Beach is a vibrant summer destination with live music every Friday night from May to September. It offers yoga, open-air theatre, beach Frisbee golf, and the National Beach Cricket Competition. Pop-up food stalls and a lively atmosphere make it a must-visit for locals and tourists.

Tolcarne Beach is a crescent bay overlooking Newquay's sea cliffs, offering scenic views, swimming, surfing, and rock pools. It's a popular spot for sea fishing and home to the 'Tolcarne Wedge' wave. The beach is accessible year-round and is part of the Great Western and Lusty Glaze beaches at low tide.
